title: Integumentary System (Skin)
shortDescription: The skin's three layers, hair, and glands, and the system's roles in protection, temperature regulation, and sensation.
genZNote: Protects, regulates, and senses — your largest organ, doing three jobs at once.

illustration.alt: Labelled cross-section illustration of the skin showing epidermis, dermis, hypodermis, hair follicle, and glands
illustration.caption: Skin (Integumentary System) — Cellfie Human Anatomy

structures.name: Dermis
structures.description: Middle layer of the skin, beneath the epidermis.
structures.function: Contains hair follicles, sweat and sebaceous glands, nerve endings, and blood vessels.

structures.name: Hypodermis (subcutaneous layer)
structures.function: Insulates the body and cushions underlying structures.

structures.name: Hair follicle
structures.description: Structure in the dermis that produces a hair shaft.

structures.name: Sebaceous gland
structures.description: Gland attached to a hair follicle.
structures.function: Secretes sebum (oil) to lubricate skin and hair.

comparisons.distinction: The epidermis is the thin, protective outer layer; the dermis beneath it holds glands, follicles, nerves, and blood vessels.
Sebaceous glands secrete oil (sebum) to lubricate skin/hair; sweat glands secrete watery sweat for cooling.

questions.prompt: In the labelled skin illustration, which layer is mostly fat and provides insulation?
questions.explanation: The hypodermis, the deepest layer, is mostly fat and insulates the body while cushioning deeper structures.
optionNotes: Thin, protective outer layer, not fat-based.
Contains glands and follicles, not primarily fat.
A gland within the dermis, not a full layer.

questions.prompt: Which gland secretes oil to lubricate skin and hair?
questions.explanation: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum (oil); sweat glands instead secrete watery sweat for cooling.
optionNotes: An endocrine gland in the neck, unrelated to skin.
An endocrine gland above the kidney, unrelated to skin.

rows: Waterproof, protective outer barrier; contains no blood vessels
Contains hair follicles, sweat glands, sebaceous glands, blood vessels, nerve endings
Fat storage and insulation, anchors skin to underlying tissue

sections.heading: Hair and Glands
bullets: Hair follicle — the structure in the dermis from which a hair shaft grows.
Hair shaft — the visible part of the hair above the skin surface.
Sebaceous gland — secretes sebum (oil) that lubricates skin and hair.
Sweat gland — produces sweat for evaporative cooling.

sections.heading: Functions
bullets: Protection — barrier against pathogens, water loss, and physical damage.
Temperature regulation — sweating cools the body; blood vessels in the dermis constrict/dilate to conserve or release heat.
Sensation — nerve endings in the dermis detect touch, pressure, temperature, and pain.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The integumentary system (skin, hair, glands) protects the body, regulates temperature, and provides sensation.
keyFacts: Three layers, outer to inner: epidermis, dermis, hypodermis.
The epidermis has no blood vessels of its own.
Sebaceous glands produce oil (sebum); sweat glands produce sweat — different secretions, different purposes.
The hypodermis is mainly fat, providing insulation and cushioning.
commonConfusion: Sebaceous glands (oil) are often confused with sweat glands (water-based sweat) — different fluids, different functions.

highYieldFacts: The epidermis is avascular (has no blood supply); nutrients diffuse up from the dermis below it.
Hair follicles and both gland types sit in the dermis, not the epidermis.
commonTraps: Don't assume the epidermis contains blood vessels — only the dermis does.
Don't merge sebaceous and sweat gland functions — one lubricates, the other cools.
mustRemember: Layer order (outer to inner): epidermis → dermis → hypodermis.
Three main functions: protection, temperature regulation, sensation.
